hook.line: Here is my very much requested engineering major tier list
hook.visual: Creator's face cut out large in the lower right over a full tier-list screenshot, with a red-outlined 'Engineering major tier list' title at top; he gestures from the first frame

beats.what: Tier list already filled in behind him; he announces it as 'very much requested'
S tier: electrical above mechanical, justified by starting pay
Explains moving computer engineering down from S to A tier because the job market is saturated
Rest of A tier: chemical, aerospace, materials, civil
Teasing jab at civil engineers ('stop saying your major is difficult')
Reassurance: every engineering major is in great shape
Predicts industrial engineering hate and puts it in B tier
Why construction engineering technology sits lower: employers read polytechnic degrees as a step down

why_it_works: A ranking is a built-in argument: every viewer has a major to defend, so the comments fill up (the caption even invites the 'biased' complaints)
The finished tier list is on screen from frame one, so viewers pause and scan for their own major before he reaches it
Calling out specific groups (civil, industrial) by name gives each group a reason to react
Fast, unbroken talking (4.8 words/s, 5% silence) over one long shot feels like a candid opinion, not a produced ad
weaknesses: 124 s with a single cut and no zooms or highlights on the tier being discussed; it relies fully on the topic
The tier-list labels are tiny and his head covers the lower tiers
Browser ads and UI clutter stay visible behind him the whole time
No captions for the speech and the audio is quiet (-27.4 LUFS)
for_robert: Steal the ranking format with a named-group callout to invite debate, but have Fred point at or circle the tier being discussed so the screen changes with each claim.
